alesis-recital-pro-mkii-who-should-buy:
Is it for you?

Who should buy the Alesis Recital Pro MKII?

Buy the Recital Pro MKII if…
✓You play now and then, not every day
✓Your budget stops at about $350
✓You want 88 weighted keys, not a 61-key keyboard
✓You mostly play chords, pop songs or with an app
✓You want to try piano before spending more
Skip it if…
✕Piano sound really matters to you
✕You plan to practice every day for years
✕You play classical pieces with lots of dynamics
✕You want Bluetooth for apps or music
✕You can stretch to about $500 (get the P-145BT)

alesis-recital-pro-mkii-accessories:
Complete the setup

What to buy with the Recital Pro MKII

SUSTAIN PEDALUpgrade first
Piano-style pedal
The included pedal is a small square footswitch that slides around. A piano-shaped pedal such as the Alesis ASP-2 feels far more natural.
STANDNeeded
X-style keyboard stand
No stand in the box. Alesis says any standard X-type stand works, no screws needed.
BENCHNeeded
Adjustable bench
Forearms level with the keys. A kitchen chair is usually too low.
HEADPHONESUseful
Any wired pair
The front jack is 1/8-inch. Use plain headphones: ones with a mic and buttons can sound wrong.
The box includes the piano, a music rest, the power adapter and the footswitch pedal.
